title: The Day the Sun Disappeared
intro: This quiz follows Anaya and Miles as they learn how a solar eclipse happens and how to observe one safely.

choices: Earth moves between the Sun and the Moon
The Moon moves between the Sun and Earth
Clouds completely cover the Sun
The Sun stops producing light
questions.explanation: A solar eclipse happens when the Moon moves between the Sun and Earth.

questions.prompt: What happens during a solar eclipse?
choices: The Moon blocks some or all of the Sun's light from reaching part of Earth
Earth blocks sunlight from reaching the Moon
The Sun moves behind Earth
The Moon produces its own light
questions.explanation: During a solar eclipse, the Moon blocks some or all of the Sun's light from reaching part of Earth.

questions.prompt: Why did the sky become darker and the air feel cooler?
choices: A storm was approaching
The Moon blocked some of the Sun's light and warmth
The Sun moved farther away
Night began earlier than usual
questions.explanation: The sky became darker and the air felt cooler because the Moon blocked some of the Sun's light and warmth.

questions.prompt: What is the safe way to look at a solar eclipse?
choices: Through ordinary sunglasses
Through binoculars
By using approved eclipse glasses
By looking directly at the Sun for only a few seconds
questions.explanation: The safe way to look at a solar eclipse is by using approved eclipse glasses.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a total and partial solar eclipse?
choices: A total eclipse blocks the entire Sun, while a partial eclipse blocks only part of it
A partial eclipse happens only at night
A total eclipse lasts all day
A partial eclipse occurs when Earth blocks the Moon
questions.explanation: In a total solar eclipse, the entire Sun is blocked; in a partial eclipse, only part of it is blocked.
